additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating large quantities of food in a discrete period while experiencing a sense of loss of control, typically accompanied by marked distress and guilt afterward. Unlike bulimia nervosa, it is not regularly followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise, and it is often associated with overweight or obesity but can occur at any weight. The course can be chronic or fluctuating, frequently emerging in the context of dieting, weight stigma, emotional stress, or long-standing patterns of using food to regulate affect. It commonly co-occurs with mood and anxiety disorders and can significantly impair psychosocial functioning and quality of life even when not perceived as severe by the individual.

patient.personality: Alixe is an organized, calm, and analytical supervisor who enjoys structure, gardening, and mindfulness practices, yet has a soft spot for indulging in new tools and small personal luxuries.
patient.stressor: Roughly five months ago, Alixe injured her knee during a weekend hike, which led to reduced mobility and her doctor advising her to significantly cut back on walking and yoga for several months. Losing her usual outlets for stress relief and physical activity was particularly destabilizing for her, given how much she relies on structured routines and movement to stay centered while managing a demanding housekeeping team. As she spent more time at home resting with her leg elevated and less time in her garden or at community clean-ups, she began cooking and snacking more out of boredom and to recreate a sense of reward after difficult days at work, often eating well beyond any physical need for food. After about four months of this pattern, she became concerned that these behaviors were persisting even as her knee improved and that they were starting to affect her energy and confidence at work, prompting her to seek psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: I’ve gotten into this pattern of eating a lot even when I know I’m not actually hungry, and it’s starting to worry me.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Lately I’ll come home after a long shift, tell myself I’m just going to have a normal dinner, and then somehow I end up eating almost an entire pan of pasta, half a loaf of garlic bread, and whatever leftovers are in the fridge in the span of an hour, way more than anyone else in my house would ever eat in one sitting.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like something in my brain just switches off—I'm watching myself go back and forth to the kitchen, thinking, 'you need to stop,' but my hand just keeps scooping food onto the plate like I’m on autopilot and not really in charge.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: There have been many nights where I eat until my stomach is so tight and bloated that I have to lie back on the couch with my leg propped up, breathing shallowly because it actually hurts to sit up straight or bend over to take off my shoes.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: I’ll finish a perfectly good lunch in the break room, feel totally full, and then as soon as I get home and put my knee up, I start wandering back to the kitchen and picking at chips, cookies, and whatever I’ve baked, not because my body needs it but because I’m restless or stressed and it’s become my go‑to distraction.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ve gotten into the habit of eating a light, ‘respectable’ amount at dinner with my boyfriend, then waiting until he goes to bed so I can quietly make a second, much bigger meal in the kitchen and eat it alone standing at the counter, because I’d be mortified if he saw how much I actually put away.
